When a translation sounds almost right

Small models often produce Japanese that is technically correct and still unpleasant to read. They mix ですます with である, over-explain conjunctions, and translate idioms that engineers never say out loud.

Patterns that give the game away

  • Batteries included becomes a lecture about batteries.
  • Move the needle is rendered as a physical needle.
  • We should probably just ship it becomes a timid stack of conditionals.

A reader on an Xteink e-ink device notices this immediately. There is no tab to switch back to English. If the prose fights them, they stop clipping.

What to preserve anyway

Command lines and package names stay in the original spelling even when the surrounding sentence is Japanese. That includes npx wrangler deploy, gpt-4o-mini, and GitHub merge-gate. 

npx wrangler deploy
npm run test:e2e

Good translation is not a knowledge-cutoff problem alone. A 2023 snapshot can still name compatibility_date. The failure mode is cadence: too many そして, しかし, and することができます in a row, until a short English post reads like a ministry circular.

Prefer a model that follows the reading-format contract without padding. If two candidates keep the code fences, pick the one that sounds like a Japanese engineer wrote the notes the same afternoon.
